## Core fitting functions

### `fit_calibrator()`

Fit a single calibration map on predictions from a separate calibration sample.

#### Required by loss

- `loss="dr"`: `mu0`, `mu1`, `propensity`
- `loss="r"`: `outcome_mean`, `propensity`

#### Common mistakes

- supplying raw learner objects instead of prediction vectors,
- forgetting `outcome_mean` for `loss="r"`,
- using non-binary treatment indicators.

### `fit_cross_calibrator()`

Use for cross-fitted treatment-effect predictions.

#### Prediction inputs

- `predictions`: pooled out-of-fold predictions used to fit the calibration map
- `fold_predictions`: `n x K` matrix used for calibrated aggregation at prediction time
- `fold_ids`: optional out-of-fold column index per observation; when supplied, the package checks that each out-of-fold prediction matches the entry in its designated column.

#### Common mistakes

- swapping `predictions` and `fold_predictions`,
- passing a single-column matrix instead of predictions from all fold-specific models,
- forgetting that prediction later also expects a fold-specific matrix.

#### Validation helpers

- `validate_crossfit_bundle(...)`: validate pooled OOF predictions, fold matrices, and optional fold IDs before fitting.
- `crossfit_bundle(...)` / `crossfit_bundle_from_data_frame(...)`: collect predictions, nuisance estimates, and fold information in one object.

### `diagnose_calibration()` {#diagnose_calibration}

Estimate a calibration curve and squared L2 calibration error, and report confidence intervals and a best linear projection of the pseudo-outcome on the score.

#### Inputs

- `predictions`, `treatment`, `outcome`, `mu0`, `mu1`, and `propensity`,
- `outcome_mean` for the overlap target (if omitted, computed from `mu0`, `mu1`, and `propensity`),
- optional comparison vector,
- optional `target_population = "dr" | "overlap" | "both"`.

#### Interpretation

Select the original or overlap-weighted population with `target_population`. See [Diagnostics](diagnostics.html) for interpretation.

### `assess_overlap()`

Summarize propensity-score tails and effective sample sizes before choosing a calibration loss.

#### Outputs

- propensity min/max,
- tail fractions below `0.05`, `0.10`, above `0.90`, `0.95` used by the default screen,
- clipped fraction,
- IPW effective sample size,
- overlap-weight effective sample size,
- severity label and recommended loss under the package defaults.

The severity label and loss recommendation use practical screening cutoffs. Choose the target population based on your scientific question.

### Bundle helpers {#bundle-helpers}

- `calibration_bundle(...)` / `calibration_bundle_from_data_frame(...)`
- `crossfit_bundle(...)` / `crossfit_bundle_from_data_frame(...)`
- `fit_bundle_calibrator(...)`
- `fit_bundle_cross_calibrator(...)`

## Fitted objects

### `Calibrator`

- `predict(...)`: apply the fitted calibration map
- `summary()`: fitting options and sample size
- plotting: visualize the fitted calibration map

### `CrossCalibrator`

- `predict(...)`: apply the map to a fold-specific matrix and aggregate with the order-statistic median
- `summary()`: metadata summary including fold count

### `CalibrationDiagnostics`

- `summary()`: scalar results, BLP slope/intercept summaries, and intervals
- plotting helpers: display the estimated calibration curve
